summary.headline: Shankesh Jewellers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 55% YoY to INR424 crore and PAT to INR43 crore, but management gave few numbers to explain the margin jump.
summary.overview: Maiden earnings call after the August 2026 listing on NSE and BSE. Revenue from operations was INR424 crore (up 55% YoY from INR273 crore), gross profit INR66 crore, EBITDA INR61 crore and PAT INR43 crore. Management attributed growth to customer relationships and product mix, while stating volumes were roughly flat YoY. Analysts repeatedly pressed for quantified margin bridges, volume data and gold-inventory gains; management mostly answered qualitatively and offered to provide more detail later.

financial_highlights.change: +55% YoY from INR273 crore; QoQ not stated
+323 bps YoY and +323 bps QoQ as stated on the call

financial_highlights.value: Approx. 14% (implied from INR61 crore / INR424 crore; analyst cited ~14%)
INR1,631 crore / INR158 crore / INR107 crore
financial_highlights.change: FY23 to FY26 3-yr revenue CAGR ~21.5%; EBITDA CAGR ~90.1%; PAT CAGR ~120%

segments.name: Corporate customers
segments.commentary: Contributed 66% of Q1 FY27 revenue, up from 55% in FY24 and 64% in FY26. Corporate clients select from company designs, and co-creation designs are billed through sales invoices, with advances given only sometimes.

segments.name: Non-corporate (single-store retail)
segments.commentary: Contributed 34% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management says the company serves around 800+ customers across India.

segments.name: 22-karat jewellery
segments.commentary: About 80% of product mix; management calls it the major driver. Bridal is said to be about 60% of sales.

segments.name: 18-karat jewellery
segments.commentary: About 20% of Q1 FY27 mix. Revenue grew from INR18 crore in FY24 to INR221 crore in FY26. Management says it earns a 'bit higher' margin than 22-karat, not a dramatically higher one.

segments.name: Geography (FY26 revenue share)
segments.commentary: West India 32%, East India 28%, South India 21%, North India 18%. Core markets are Maharashtra, Bihar, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 55% YoY growth is volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were approximately the same YoY, so growth came from product mix and customer relationships. No quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin, given EBITDA of about 14% in Q1 after 9.5% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins move quarter to quarter with product mix and that the company focuses on profit amount rather than percentage. It did not commit to a sustainable margin range.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price risk hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: The company buys gold equal to what it sells on the same day at market price. Inventory is carried at a weighted-average cost that management says is below market, so no hedging is needed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion comes from product mix and how much from inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix was one factor and gold-price gains add 1-3 percentage points YoY. Analysts disputed that Q1 had gold gains, and management gave no split.

qa_highlights.question: How is growth funded and what is the working-capital cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Profits are reinvested, and the bank lines are open. The IPO raised equity to about INR450 crore to fund working capital. Management said the business needs more working capital as it grows.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers moving karigar work in-house, and what is the moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said handcrafted, co-created bridal designs and long-standing relationships protect the business. It gave no figures to show the moat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did job-worker count fall and employee cost drop QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers larger, organised contract manufacturers. Employee cost fell because Q4 included an ex-gratia payment to directors, which will not recur.

risks_watch: Margin sustainability: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin of about 14% vs 9.5% in Q4 FY26; management gave no sustainable range and said margins move with product mix. Track next quarter's gross and EBITDA margin against this base.

Unquantified growth drivers: 55% revenue growth attributed to mix and relationships with volumes described only as 'approximately same'; volume split and gold-price contribution (management cited 1-3 pp YoY) were not quantified. Watch for the promised Q2/Q3 volume data.

Working capital and funding: trade receivables of INR126 crore (about 22-23 days), inventory turnover about 8x, and management saying working capital needs keep growing; IPO proceeds (INR38 crore working-capital portion) are a key use to track against bank line usage.

Customer in-housing and moat: analysts questioned whether large customers such as Kalyan and P.N. Gadgil moving to in-house karigars threatens the outsourced model; management gave no share or retention figures.

Gold-price hedging and inventory accounting: hedging relies on a same-day buy-to-sell policy and weighted-average inventory valued below market; management did not show the inventory gain component, which analysts disputed for Q1.

summary.management_tone: Confident on the business narrative (handcrafted bridal, co-creation, asset-light karigar network) but evasive on quantification: repeatedly deferred volume, margin-bridge and product-mix numbers to future quarters or a separate call. Answers on hedging, funding and capacity were firmer, while management said it would provide figures later.
